A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LVSM research, with matching architectures, equations and principal experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, architecture and depth ablations, zero-shot generalization results and rendering-speed measurements, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds GSO encoder-decoder depth-allocation results and tokenizer/attention ablations in Tables 2-3.

M1.justification: Both versions propose the same encoder-decoder and decoder-only architectures, Plucker-ray patch tokenization, full self-attention and rendering losses in Equations 1-8. The new diagrams and latent-token count disclose implementation details; the added architectural variants are ablations, not revisions to the proposed models.

E1.justification: Both use Objaverse for object-level training, GSO and ABO for object evaluation, and RealEstate10K for scene experiments. The varying-input-view studies remain. New ablations reuse existing coverage, and the expanded limitations do not establish a separately added evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same external baselines. Within Table 3, v2 adds comparison variants using a CNN tokenizer, encoder-decoder per-patch prediction and a pure cross-attention decoder. The SRT-inspired components are evaluated as LVSM variants; a complete SRT baseline is not newly reported.

E3.justification: The added GSO experiments introduce controlled tokenizer and attention substitutions and encoder/decoder layer allocations with 24 total layers. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and primary training schedules remain unchanged. Explicit ablation batch sizes are additional documentation, not evidence that retained experiments changed settings or were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 substantially expands architectural testing: CNN tokenization, joint target-patch updating in the encoder-decoder model and a pure cross-attention decoder are newly examined. Encoder/decoder depth allocation is also tested on GSO. The earlier GSO decoder-depth study is retained through consolidation of v1 Table 4 into v2 Table 2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, result variability or statistical significance tests. The new result rows retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands architecture results. Table 2 adds GSO encoder-decoder PSNRs of 26.48, 25.69 and 24.74 for the 6+18, 12+12 and 18+6 allocations. Table 3 adds CNN, per-patch and pure-cross-attention results of 27.59, 26.27 and 24.60 dB versus the retained 28.07 dB reference. CNN LPIPS is slightly better, 0.052 versus 0.053, despite lower PSNR and SSIM. Existing benchmark scores, plotted curves and relocated decoder-depth results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical model and loss definitions in Equations 1-8 are retained. New attention diagrams and discussions of deterministic prediction provide conceptual explanations, without new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: two architectures with minimal 3D inductive bias, the quality-versus-speed tradeoff, zero-shot input-view generalization and strong performance with limited training resources. Added supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices A.6-A.7 add substantial reasoning about deterministic versus generative view consistency and explicitly acknowledge noisy, flickering predictions in unseen regions. Section 4.4 expands explanations of tokenization and attention mechanisms. The aspect-ratio limitation is retained from v1 A.2, while v1 A.4's camera-baseline explanation for different object/scene scaling behavior is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 3072 latent tokens, model parameter counts, ablation batch sizes of 64 and 256, and the 256-by-256 setting for rendering-speed measurements. Figure 8 documents normalization placement and detailed token flow. Most training and optimizer details are retained or relocated; these disclosures do not establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning relative to SRT and introduces a dedicated comparison with generative NVS in Appendix A.6. Added references include ViewFormer, 3DiM, Zero-1-to-3, Free3D, EscherNet, CAT3D and SV3D, supporting discussion of camera control, consistency and inductive biases. Updates to existing Transformer and BERT references are bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Section 4.4 is extensively reorganized into tokenization, fixed-length encoding and bidirectional-attention discussions. The naming explanation moves from Section 3.2 to Appendix A.1, and detailed training settings move to A.2. The appendix is reorganized around architectural explanations, generative-model comparisons and limitations, alongside widespread language editing.

P2.justification: v2 adds detailed architecture and attention-mask diagrams as Figures 8-9. Table 2 combines the former scene-depth and appendix object-depth tables, adding GSO encoder results and parameter-count columns; Table 3 gains comparison rows. Table 1 and several figures are repositioned, while the original Figures 1-7 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The added controlled ablations strengthen support for architectural choices, while explicit latent-token counts, detailed diagrams and unseen-region limitations improve reproducibility and clarity. The established benchmark findings remain unchanged. Some broader consistency claims in Appendix A.6 rely partly on external videos and lack quantitative support within the PDFs, limiting the demonstrated gain. Overall, v2 provides a better-supported and more transparent account of the existing contribution.
